---
title: "Workflow"
---

How the project goes from inputs to the paper.

## Stages

1. **Plan:** write `docs/protocol.qmd`, commit it and run
   `just freeze-protocol` before any confirmatory analysis.
2. **Acquire:** place source data in `data/external/` and record each file
   in `provenance.yml`.
3. **Prepare:** transform it through `data/interim/` into `data/processed/`.
4. **Analyse:** run the analysis, writing outputs of stochastic or external
   systems to `results/raw/` and deterministic outputs to `results/derived/`.
5. **Report:** generate `results/tables/`, `results/figures/` and
   `results/variables.yml`.
6. **Write:** render the paper in `paper/` from those outputs.

Stages 3 to 5 run from code in `src/research/` or `scripts/`, never from a
notebook, and implement the protocol or a documented amendment.

## Commands

Run the `just` targets; `just --list` shows them all. Each uses the locked
environment in `uv.lock`. To change dependencies, edit `pyproject.toml` and
run `uv lock`.

| Command                | What it does                                                          |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `just setup`           | Install the locked environment.                                       |
| `just check`           | Formatting, lint, types and unit tests. Fast; needs no Quarto.        |
| `just analyse`         | Run the canonical analysis. The project defines it.                   |
| `just verify`          | Protocol lock, repository and notebook integrity, render, manuscript. |
| `just render`          | Render the documents and paper to HTML.                               |
| `just pdf`             | Render the paper to PDF. Needs a TeX installation.                    |
| `just prose`           | Run Vale on `paper/` and `docs/`. Needs Vale; not run in CI.          |
| `just freeze-protocol` | Freeze the protocol. Runs once.                                       |

Analysis, verification and rendering are separate. `just check` and
`just verify` never run the analysis; they check what it produced.

## Protocol and amendments

`protocol/manifest.toml` lists the files to freeze. `just freeze-protocol`
refuses unless they are committed, then writes `protocol/lock.json` with the
time, the commit, the file set and their SHA-256 hashes. Commit the lock.

After the freeze, the frozen files and the lock never change, and the
protocol cannot be frozen again, even after the lock is deleted. `just verify`
checks that the lock is byte-identical to the lock as first committed, that
it agrees with the manifest, that its commit is in the history, that the
files at that commit match the hashes and that the files on disk still do. It
needs the full Git history and fails in a shallow clone. Record every later change to the plan as an amendment in
`docs/amendments/`.

## Exploratory work

Notebooks in `notebooks/` and outputs in `results/exploratory/` are
exploratory. Nothing canonical reads from them, and the paper reports them,
if at all, as exploratory. To make an exploratory result canonical, move the
code into `src/research/` or `scripts/`, justify it from the protocol or an
amendment and regenerate it there.

## Generated artifacts

Everything under `data/interim/`, `data/processed/` and `results/`, except
`results/raw/`, is generated by code and can be regenerated by
`just analyse`. Accepted outputs in `results/raw/` are preserved as
produced. The template does not enforce this: a project that relies on them
adds its own provenance records and integrity checks. Small
publication-facing artifacts, such as
`results/variables.yml`, tables and figures, may be committed so that changes
show in review. They stay regenerable; never edit them by hand. Decide per
project whether to commit larger generated files, and add them to
`.gitignore` if not.

## References

`paper/references.bib` is a controlled artifact. New entries are added
deliberately, never while drafting.

1. Export the entry from an authoritative record: the DOI resolver, the
   publisher or a reference manager. For a DOI,
   `curl -LH "Accept: application/x-bibtex" https://doi.org/<doi>`.
   Never type an entry from memory.
2. Add it as its own change and compare it with the source: authors, title,
   year, venue, DOI.
3. Run `just verify`. It checks that the file parses, keys are unique, every
   citation resolves and DOIs are well formed. It does not check that a DOI
   exists.

While drafting, mark a missing source as `[CITATION NEEDED: <what>]`.
`just verify` fails while any remain.

## Values in the manuscript

Numbers cited in prose are generated, not typed.

1. Have the analysis write the value to `results/variables.yml`, rounded and
   formatted. The file is YAML; nested mappings become dotted keys.
2. Cite it with `{{{< meta key >}}}`, for example
   `{{{< meta sample.n >}}}`.

A missing or misspelled key renders as `?meta:key`. Quarto only warns, so
`just verify` checks the rendered output and fails on any that remain. It
also warns about text in `paper/` that looks like a statistical result typed
by hand.
